utterances.text: [Music] all too often a spindle is replaced without getting to the root cause of the
problem which leads to another failure down the road so before you go through the trouble of
replacing your spindle let's stop and do some troubleshooting to rule out any other issues
here we have a spindle that's seized and quit running but what caused it to seize most often
the root causes lubrication as in the spindle is not getting enough oil pay particular attention
if your machine has a busier pump as they age these pumps can sometimes work intermittently
so even a successful lube test is no guarantee that the Pope is good these pumps should always
be rebuilt when a spindle problem is suspected and if the pump is over five years old a rebuild
us necessary anyway check out Hoss parts comm or the rebuild kit that includes the gear motor and
don't skip this step and if you've got one of these older pumps that's using either back for
two or G t25 oils switch those out for our current spec oils either Mobil SH c6 25 or a high quality
synthetic 5w 20 Automotive type oil both of these are direct replacements if your machine has a hoss
metering valve style pump check for air leaks and bubbles inside the tank at the bottom of the
valve body and the tube that carries oil into the sight glass if you can see air bubbles the
pump isn't properly lubricating the spindle also be sure and check for oil leaks at the
sight glass if oil is leaking here the spindle is not being properly lubricated remember if
any of these problems are not corrected your new spindle will seize just like the old one
now let's talk about a spindle that is running hot the most common reason for this is too much
oil reaching the spindle check your lubrication system and make sure that the proper amount of oil
is being delivered the procedure for this varies depending on machine model and pump type refer to
the documentation for your pump that's available at DIY hasti and see calm and follow the proper
teacher fixing this will most likely correct the problem and will save you from replacing
the spindle next let's consider a spindle with a noise or vibration problem before replacing
the spindle always check to make sure that your tooling isn't the problem and that the spindle
is balanced properly we have a video that covers that procedure on an inline spindle make sure that
the spindle and motor are properly aligned this is also covered in our spindle balancing video
if your spindle is belt driven make sure that the belt tension is correct and that the belts
and sprockets are clean and in good condition last let's talk about a spindle where the tool
is sticking when dealing with a stuck tool the spindle is rarely the problem it's much more
likely that it has to do with the tools being used and the application really long or heavy
tools can lead to the tool fretting in the taper you should take a careful look at any applications
using these types of tools to ensure they aren't contributing to the problem also go back and take
another look at the spindle temperature tools are more likely to stick in a hot spindle deal with
the lubrication problem we talked about earlier and you will probably solve your tool sticking
problem as well one last note if the drive dogs or spindle taper has been damaged by an orientation
problem this must be corrected before you replace the spindle bottom line spindle troubles offer
the result of a host of external issues with just a little troubleshooting there's a good
chance you can solve the problem and be back up and running in no time thanks for watching you
